name: Chorti
catalog_citation: Wisdom, Charles. 1940. The Chorti Indians of Guatemala. Chicago: University of Chicago Press (archive.org item chortiindiansofg031696mbp, scanned text). Supporting: Comunidad Linguistica Ch'orti' / ALMG, Gramatica Descriptiva del idioma maya Ch'orti', sec. 1.2.7 …
catalog_locator: Wisdom 1940, Author's Preface pp. viii-x (stress sentence p. x); ALMG sec. 1.2.7; Marhenke 2015/2021 Preface (PDF pp. 4-5)
catalog_quote: Wisdom 1940, Author's Preface: "Results of studies in the Chorti language will appear in a separate publication; but, since some Chorti terms are mentioned in the text, a description of the phonetic alphabet employed will be useful. ... Diphthongs consist of a, e, and o plus i or u, and of u plus i, with stress on the first element (falling diphthongs), even when final or before final x or h ... The glottal stop, after and between vowels, is very weak; vowel plus glottal stop seems to vary freely with long vowel, with a faint rearticulation after the glottal stop ... Stress is always on the last syllable and is unmarked." ALMG Gramatica Descriptiva 1.2.7: "Entre algunas formas de acentuación que se encuentran en los idiomas mayas están: a) Algunos se acentúan en la sílaba más pesada de cada palabra. b) Otras se acentúa en la última vocal de cada palabra, considerándose como sílaba tónic…

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: Wisdom 1940's 'Stress is always on the last syllable and is unmarked' and the falling-diphthong sentence are verbatim in the held archive.org scanned at Author's Preface pp. ix-x; ALMG 2004 sec. 1.2.7 and Marhenke's preface are verbatim in copies we hold, and a clean native-text ALMG PDF downloaded now shows the same passage (PDF p. 29-30). The weakness is the kind of deciding source, not its content: an ethnographer's phonetic note (1940) plus a community grammar sketch. But a better source is already held by the project and simply not cited in the stress record: Dugan 2013 (Tulane PhD, held as the morph source) sec. 2.4 pp. 26-27 states final stress, explicitly weight-blind ('weight doesn't determine the location of stress'), with penultimate stress only in loans (ilama < Nahuatl, kilis < Sp. eclipse) and notes (3.4.10.1) that enclitic -ka can carry the stress.
